text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian neuwspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Police arrested managers of two pyramid investment companies and 50 of their staff.
- Unconfirmed reports say wives of some senior officials have been seen withdrawing money from some pyramid scheme companies whose managers were arrested a day later.
- The small right-wing National Front Party calls for the government's resignation.
- Greek ambassador Costantinos Prevedurakis said the collapse of the pyramid schemes could push many Albanians towards illegally crossing the border to Greece in another wave of immigration.
- Hundreds of depositors in the southern city of Lushnje held a protest on Wednesday asking for their money back.
- Scores of foreign citizens -- Greeks, Italians, Bulgarians -- have come to Albania worried about their deposits at some pyramid schemes.

- Cenaj & Co, one of the pyramid scheme investment firms, decided to stop its operation by giving back all deposits to investors. Two other companies have done the same but returned only 20 percent of the invested deposits.
- A scheme financier said about 1.5 million depositors had invested $200 million at Xhaferri foundation.
- Prosecutor's office questioned some opposition leaders on last Sunday's protest at Skanderbeg Square.
